purpose: Screen book-inspired money-mindset topics for genuinely distinct editorial angles. Ideas are paraphrased in original wording; no direct quotations are included.
screening_basis: Compared against the 42 existing mindset blueprints before adding three distinct decision-quality topics. A book listing verifies bibliographic identity and broad subject only; it does not prove every script claim. Claim-level review remains mandatory.

accepted_candidates.title: When you have already spent money, walking away can still be wise
accepted_candidates.reason: Sunk-cost thinking and escalation of commitment are not directly covered by the current topic set. Keep the lesson focused on future costs and choices, not shame.

accepted_candidates.title: A good money decision can still have a bad outcome
accepted_candidates.reason: Separates decision quality from outcome under uncertainty; distinct from general patience, risk awareness and setback recovery.

accepted_candidates.title: Do not mistake a lucky result for a reliable money strategy
accepted_candidates.reason: Focuses on luck versus skill and the danger of extrapolating from one success; distinct from avoiding get-rich-quick offers or financial trends.

screened_out.title: Why you keep spending because you already paid
screened_out.reason: Same sunk-cost angle as accepted topic; retained only one clear title.

screened_out.title: Why one lucky investment does not make you an expert
screened_out.reason: Same luck-versus-skill lesson as accepted topic.

screened_out.title: Why a bad result does not always mean a bad decision
screened_out.reason: Same decision-quality-versus-outcome lesson as accepted topic.

screened_out.title: Why following the crowd feels safer with money
screened_out.reason: Overlaps existing trend-following and comparison-trap blueprints.

screened_out.title: Why a bonus feels easier to spend than a salary
screened_out.reason: Overlaps existing windfall and payday-spending topics.

screened_out.title: Why we fear losses more than we value gains
screened_out.reason: Needs a more distinct practical angle; overlaps financial setbacks and fear-based decision avoidance.

screened_out.title: Why confidence can become overconfidence
screened_out.reason: Overlaps money-confidence and trend-following topics; may be revisited with a sharply distinct investing-risk brief.

editorial_safeguards: No direct quotations from copyrighted modern books or speeches.
Use the author's name and book title only when bibliographic identity is verified.
Write every explanation independently; do not imitate distinctive prose.
Do not present a book as scientific proof; source and verify factual claims separately.
Every generated script remains a candidate pending claim-level and editorial review.
